topics.topic: Failure classification and concealment for unavailable stored binary content
questions: Which exact failure class must each object kind return for missing, oversize or unlisted stored content?
When an otherwise authorized expense document's source object is missing, must the caller receive the concealed document-not-found response or an explicit storage-unavailable response?

quotes:
An unknown, cross-project or hidden read is answered the same way, so the caller cannot tell them apart; a refused document read answers that way also when its stored content is missing, oversize or unlisted, while a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered fails as an explicit storage-unavailable error (Factory
`babd5e52`, `rules.binary_delivery_policy`; Factory code
`domain/photo_management.py`; owner 2026-11-06: current service behaviour
accepted; technical decisions delegated).
judgement.why: This is the same document-versus-photo binary-failure question already judged in P13, and neither the quoted passage nor the email-challenge change altered it.

`babd5e52`, `rules.binary_delivery_policy`; Factory code
`domain/photo_management.py`; owner 2026-11-06: current service behaviour

topics.topic: Whether missing progress records contribute zero or make progress unavailable
questions: For a section with planned work but no SectionProgress record, is its completed-work value unavailable or exactly zero?
When the active budget has positive planned work but no section has a progress record, is overall progress unavailable or zero?

quotes:
A section without a record has no
  recorded progress: its views show `completion_percent = None` and a
  completed work value of zero, never an invented 0 %.

Overall progress: `Σ(work_planned × percent) / Σ(work_planned)` over
  sections of the active version with `work_planned > 0` and a recorded
  progress (a section without a progress record is left out of both sums);
  undefined (shown unavailable) when the denominator is 0.
judgement.why: Both missing-progress rules were unchanged when the state was reopened, and removing email challenges did not make either rule newly material.

provenance.quote: A section without a record has no recorded progress: its views show completion_percent = None and a completed work value

topics.topic: Expiry timing for a replaced service credential during rotation
questions: When a replacement service credential is issued, what determines when the previous credential stops working?

quotes:
The `PortalStore`, the administrator's `StaffActorContext`, the principal id
and an optional `expires_at`. Any expiry is accepted and stored as
supplied, a past one included, never converted (A28 keeps a supplied time); no expiry means the credential does not expire. A
credential is usable only before its expiry, so one issued with an expiry
already reached is stored but never authenticates.

A12, A17 (a 32-byte secret, the source-fixed A30 entropy of
`create_runtime_app`, issued for the fresh `credential_id`; only the hash
stored); earlier credentials stay valid until revoked; A13
(`principal.credential_issue` naming the new credential as entity, with
its key version).
judgement.why: This is the same credential-rotation overlap question already judged in P12, and the email-challenge change affected none of its passages.

credential is usable only before its expiry, so one issued with an expiry
already reached is stored but never authenticates.

A12, A17 (a 32-byte secret, the source-fixed A30 entropy of
`create_runtime_app`, issued for the fresh `credential_id`; only the hash
stored); earlier credentials stay valid until revoked; A13
(`principal.credential_issue` naming the new credential as entity, with
its key version).
precedent.why: The later operation contract says issuance leaves earlier credentials valid until explicit revocation and permits the caller to bound overlap with expires_at or leave the credential non-expiring.

topics.topic: Response format and typed error for refused expense commands
questions: When an otherwise valid confirmed expense publication uses a non-EUR currency, does the caller receive a typed `currency_mismatch` error or an untyped empty 422 response?
Are command-error responses required to be JSON, or may expense validation failures return an empty non-JSON response?

quotes:
Currency literal: `EUR` only; any other currency at any boundary →
  explicit typed rejection (`currency_mismatch`).

Every refusal before the replay check answers
HTTP 422 with an empty body (`rules.http_router_backend.error_policy`), so
which of them failed first is not observable to the caller; a replay with
other content is the conflict of A8 (409).
judgement.why: The internal currency-rejection rule and external empty-422 rule were both unchanged, and the email-challenge removal did not affect expense error responses.

topics.topic: Validation order between an expense and replacement allocations during standalone re-allocation
questions: After the project guard passes, does standalone re-allocation validate the expense first or the replacement allocations first?

quotes:
Once the route's project guard of A4 has passed, an expense
correction checks its total first, then the expense, then the allocation instructions
(non-empty, sum, then each section target) (Factory code `domain/expense_management.py`
`correct_expense`); a refused total or allocation answers 422, an expense
of no or another project 409.
judgement.why: The passage specifying validation order for correction while leaving standalone re-allocation at issue was unchanged, and the email-challenge change did not affect expense allocation operations.

topics.topic: Where normalized OCR item semantic validation occurs relative to authentication and project guarding
questions: Are M24/M25 semantic item constraints enforced during request decoding before authentication, or by the authenticated OCR adapter/use case after the project guard?

quotes:
`NormalizedRecognitionItem` is the portal-owned minimum OCR boundary item:
  `line_id: str`, `description: str`, `quantity: Decimal (> 0)`,
  `unit_price: Decimal (>= 0)`, `line_total: Decimal (>= 0)`.
  Line IDs are unique within one publication. The portal validates presence
  and decimal shape but does not recompute Expense total from items because
  receipt-level taxes/discounts may not be itemized; items are discarded after
  boundary validation in the MVP.
judgement.why: The OCR-item validation passage was unchanged, and removing staff email challenges did not alter expense request decoding or project authorization.

topics.topic: Whether audit append failure rolls back the associated business mutation
questions: Must every audited business mutation roll back when its AuditRecord cannot be appended?

quotes:
- **Audit.** A significant success and its audit record commit in one
  transaction through `audit_writer.append_audit` (A13, A23); an idempotent
  replay writes no second creation audit. The audited action, result, reason
  and `entity_id` are the operation's to build.
judgement.why: This is the same audit-failure atomicity question already judged in P4, and neither its deciding later-state passage nor the relevant State 2 text changed.

precedent.topic: Audit failure rollback versus unaudited business commit
quotes:
- **Audit.** A significant success and its audit record commit in one
  transaction through `audit_writer.append_audit` (A13, A23); an idempotent
  replay writes no second creation audit. The audited action, result, reason
  and `entity_id` are the operation's to build.
precedent.why: State 5 requires the business mutation and its audit record to commit in one transaction, so an audit persistence failure prevents the mutation from committing.

topics.topic: Whether missing Registry configuration causes startup failure or deferred operational failure
questions: Must a deployment without REGISTRY_BASE_URL fail startup, or may it start and fail only when a Registry operation is attempted?

quotes:
`REGISTRY_BASE_URL` is read by the Registry
gateway at each call, not at start-up: it is no required start-up variable,
and its absence fails only Registry calls (A6).
judgement.why: This is the same Registry configuration startup question already judged in P2, and the quoted passage was unchanged by the email-challenge removal.

precedent.topic: Registry base URL startup requirement versus deferred failure
quotes:
`REGISTRY_BASE_URL` is read by the Registry
gateway at each call, not at start-up: it is no required start-up variable,
and its absence fails only Registry calls (A6).
precedent.why: A30 explicitly permits startup without REGISTRY_BASE_URL and makes its absence fail only a later Registry call.

topics.topic: Whether monetary inputs with excess fractional digits are rejected or rounded
questions: At an external input boundary, must a finite EUR Decimal with more than two fractional digits be rejected, or rounded half-up to two digits?

quotes:
The amount quantized to two digits, ROUND_HALF_UP. An amount with more
fraction digits is rounded, never refused, and the sign rule is applied to
the rounded amount.
judgement.why: This is the same excess-fraction monetary-input question already judged in P11, and its deciding later-state passage was unaffected by the change.
